rows.name: Totient chain: K_i = C_(i-1) + phi(p_n), skip-on-repeat
rows.rationale: The one number stream the author actually published (section 0.16, f(n)=phi(n) over the primes) but used in the chain form the book's later sections hint at ('numbers are the direction'): each rune is keyed by its predecessor plus the next totient. The lag-1 difference stream is then exactly a totient Vigenere of the plaintext, so lag-1 classes, unigram and IC all stay flat (the totient residues are near-uniform), and a doublet needs phi(p_n) = -P_i, which the author's rejection loop skips four times in five. LZ and WZ swept the chain only rigidly; phase 3 ran the totient only in plain Vigenere form. The skip decoder has never been pointed at the first-difference stream. No F rule: any literal F would push F to twice its share and the pages' unigram chi-square of 26 forbids it.

rows.name: Prime chain, Beaufort sign: C_i = K_i - P_i with K_i = C_(i-1) + p_n
rows.rationale: Same chain idea with the raw prime stream (the 'stream of prime numbers' of the published key) and the one sign combination the chain sweeps did not pair with skip: Beaufort. Under Beaufort a doublet requires p_n = 2C_(i-1) - ... effectively a different rejection set, so a decoder built for C = P + K misses it even on the difference stream. Statistically it is indistinguishable from rank 1 at the gate (flat everywhere, doublets governed by the soft skip), which is the point: the gate cannot choose among signs, the decoder must. Primes mod 29 never hit residue 0, a 1/29 hole that the plaintext convolution washes out of the unigram.

rows.name: Plaintext autokey over the totient stream (K_i = P_(i-1) + phi(p_n))
rows.rationale: The book's own polyalphabetic method with the plaintext folded in: the previous clear rune is added to the published totient stream. Pure plaintext autokey fails the gate because P_i + P_(i-1) is far from flat, but adding a flat deterministic stream restores a flat unigram and a flat lag-1 difference spectrum (the differences are P_i - P_(i-2) plus totient gaps). Doublets occur when P_i - P_(i-2) equals a totient gap, independent of the key's history, so the soft skip delivers 1/5 of 445. WZ's 48 PT-feedback configs and LZ's plaintext lags 1-3 were run without a base stream and without the skip; this is the untried corner that still only needs the published key.

rows.name: Cicada LCG mod 3301 (a = 1033, c = 0), key = x mod 29, skip-on-repeat
rows.rationale: The author is 'machine not hand' (WZ, power 0.99) and loves 3301 and 1033; a multiplicative congruential generator modulo the prime 3301 is the simplest publishable 'numbers are the direction' pad. Its residues mod 29 are flat to the gate, its period (a divisor of 3300) exceeds every page, each page starts from a different seed (so no shared keystream at any alignment, as observed), and a code loop that redraws on a repeated output with a random-looking 81 percent (e.g. a secondary test on the generator state) is exactly the signature. WZ's PRNG rounds covered MT and KDF seeds, never small modular generators with Cicada constants; the seed space per page is 3300, trivially exhaustive for a decoder.

rows.name: Probe: hard anti-repeat (p = 1) with the published literal-F rule as the only le
rows.rationale: The one way a deliberate, hard 'never repeat' rule could still leave 86 doublets is a channel the rule does not inspect, and the author's own channel is the unencrypted plaintext F that consumes no key. Doublets then arise only where a cipher F precedes a literal F or two literal Fs abut, which I estimate at 15-25, and the literal Fs should push the F count to about twice its share and break the unigram chi-square of 26. I expect the gate to reject it on both columns; a rejection is useful because it rules out the hard rule for good and, with it, the F rule on the unsolved pages.

The extra stream prevents the ciphertext difference from simply exposing shifted plaintext, while nonlinear feedback may dilute the totient stream's residual structure. rows.name: Prime-gap key with a clock-dependent affine multiplier
rows.rationale: This is a deliberate boundary probe of the independent-additive-key reading, not another prime, prime-minus-one, or prime-plus-one offset sweep. Prime gaps retain the author's prime-number vocabulary, while the position-dependent invertible coefficient changes how plaintext differences interact with the numerical stream. The explicitly changed construction is a prime-gap key combined with a changing affine coefficient under soft rejection; the supplied ledger does not identify that combination. The gap distribution alone is strongly nonuniform, so a plain additive gap key would be a poor candidate. Here the multiplier cycle is intended to average that bias, giving a provisional prediction near 87 doublets. rows.name: 3301-LCG in Beaufort, soft cipher skip
rows.rationale: Same finite pad as the leading proposal — the phase-2 independent key plus an 81 percent redraw, modulus 3301 so each page is a 3301-seed search — but Beaufort, C=K−P, rather than add. Phase 4 existed because this repository had only decrypted P=C−K, and neither sign of (a, c, m)=(7, 1, 3301) has been run; the other three ledgers treat the sign as part of the construction. A uniform key hits the doublet congruence once in 29 under either sign, and the skip then cuts that rate to about 86, which is why round 1's Beaufort LCG row passed the other three columns as well. No F-rule, skip not bump.

rows.name: rune-prime feedback on a 3301-LCG, soft skip
rows.rationale: Round 1's prime_value ciphertext feedback plus an LCG passed all four but sat on a 2^31 modulus, which is not a sweep. Shrinking the base to x→7x+1 mod 3301 keeps the whitening a structured stream lacks and cuts the family to 3301 seeds. The feedback term is the Gematria prime, not the identity map already gated on totient and prime bases, and the repeat rule is skip so a rejection advances the LCG instead of substituting a secret symbol. That is outside WZ's 48 feedback configs, which had no LCG base and no soft skip, and outside the named-PRNG sweeps.

rows.name: solved-text running key plus rune-prime feedback, skip by two
rows.rationale: The book keys itself: both solved word keys were taken from its plaintext, and phase 3 already ran that plaintext as a running key at all 2,977 offsets under single skip, null. A naked running key fails the unigram at z=−13; round 1 showed that adding a Gematria-prime feedback term brings the same base inside all four statistics (lag-1 z=−0.7). The change from that row is skip k=2 rather than one redraw: phase 7 ran skip-by-two on the book families and found the single-advance decoder misses those plants, but not on a running key mixed with prime_value feedback. Finite offsets, decryptable, no F-rule.
